agenda_items.title: Presentation IR (PIR) — Capability-Bound Interaction Graph Compiler
agenda_items.intent_description: Define Presentation IR as a capability-bound interaction graph — not a traditional UI schema but a compiled projection of a capability-constrained service graph into interaction surfaces under identity-scoped validity rules. PIR is generated via a 7-step compilation algorithm using constrained graph clustering: (1) represent capabilities as typed weighted graph with domain/intent/object/behavioral co-use signals, (2) build capability affinity graph, (3) run constrained clustering by cohesion/intent consistency/object locality/LOSM validity, (4) view archetype assignment (graph/table/form), (5) view boundary normalization to prevent UI explosion, (6) action extraction mapping capabilities to interactions, (7) PIR emission as JSON-structured view assembly.
requirements: Step 1: Represent capabilities as typed weighted graph (domain, intent, object, behavioral co-use)
Step 2: Build Capability Affinity Graph from weighted edges
Step 3: Constrained clustering — cohesion, intent consistency, object locality, LOSM validity
Step 4: Rule-based view archetype assignment (graph, table, form)
Step 5: View boundary normalization — split large clusters, suppress duplicates
Step 6: Action extraction — map individual capabilities to interaction actions
Step 7: PIR emission — JSON-structured view assembly
implementation_notes: Core philosophy: UI is just the renderer of that projection — the system is a capability-to-perception compiler for distributed systems
PIR is compiled, not designed — same capabilities always produce same PIR
This eliminates UI design drift — the UI surface is deterministically derived from the capability graph
open_questions: What is the formal clustering algorithm — Louvain, Leiden, or custom constrained optimization?
How are view archetypes extended when new interaction patterns emerge — new rules or new archetypes?
